node: Data-center electrical equipment: switchgear, transformers, busway, backup power, and power distribution
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe for the data-center electrical-equipment node. The strongest evidence in this pass is not from AI narratives but from hard order/backlog signals: Powell Industries disclosed multiple data-center infrastructure orders, including a post-quarter order above $400 million, while Vertiv provides the obvious reference exposure through power management, switchgear, busbar, UPS, rack power distribution, and integrated data-center infrastructure. The underfollowed lane is narrower than the broad AI-infrastructure story suggests: Powell, IES Holdings, and Atkore each have plausible direct or second-order exposure, but they require different validation paths. Powell is the cleanest order/backlog signal; IES is an execution-services and electrical-systems beneficiary; Atkore is a lower-conviction component/channel exposure that needs data-center mix verification. Layer 1B expansion finds a narrow but investable US-listed universe around AI/data-center electrical equipment. The strongest underfollowed direct signal is Powell Industries, where record backlog, high book-to-bill, and a disclosed data-center mega-order tie the AI buildout to medium-voltage switchgear and engineered electrical systems. nVent is a broader but still relatively less-obvious electrical connection/protection and busway/switchgear exposure, strengthened by its Avail Electrical Products acquisition and record 2026 backlog. Vertiv remains the high-attention reference leader for critical power/cooling infrastructure. AZZ is a second-order materials/services candidate
